2) Confirmation on whether the private offer can fix the list unit price per 1M tokens (so we can commit a spend band) and whether any committed volume discounts are represented in the Marketplace price or as a separate contractual credit.

Elaine — thanks, great questions and thanks for the clear usage range. High-level answers below and attaching a concise pricing_matrix.csv for modeling.

Quick summary: 
- Marketplace unit: 1 unit = 1M tokens for the private offer (Marketplace product line item).
- Marketplace fee: AWS Marketplace takes a percentage on the Marketplace list price in the private offer flow (usually 15–20% depending on agreement). For modeling we used 20% as a conservative assumption.
- Mapping example (we'll include these rows in the CSV): 
  • AWS marketplace list price: $410 / 1M tokens
  • Marketplace fee (20%): $82 / 1M tokens
  • Redwood net receipt: $328 / 1M tokens (what Redwood invoices to AWS and receives after fee).

Committed discounts: We can represent committed volume in two ways: 
- Option A (Marketplace price): we put the committed unit price directly in the private offer listing (simpler for procurement; AWS bills the committed unit price).
- Option B (Contract + credits): sign a Redwood contract outside the Marketplace for committed volume; Marketplace shows a nominal list price and we apply credits/invoice adjustments off-platform.

Recommendation: Option A (private offer list price fixed) is cleaner for your procurement and keeps billing through AWS. It also lets us set a ramped pricing ladder (eg $420 for 0–50M, $395 for 50–150M, $365 for 150M+).

Request from our side: can you confirm the target per-1M price you want encoded in the private offer and whether you want a ramp/tiers? Also confirm preferred PO/billing contact and if procurement will sign via DocuSign.

Attachments: pricing_matrix.csv (example mappings + tiers)

I'll loop Marissa (cc) for the PO draft and DocuSign link once we have the exact target unit price.

Thanks — Karthik

Hi Elaine — thanks for confirming. Attached is a PO draft (PixlMedia_PO_draft_8672.pdf) and a one-page mapping note below that you can attach to your supplier record. I've also pushed a DocuSign envelope to the link we shared.

One-page mapping note (for procurement):
- Marketplace unit: 1M tokens = 1 Marketplace line-item unit.
- Private offer unit price (AWS list price): $395 / 1M tokens (as confirmed by PixlMedia).
- Marketplace fee estimate: 20% of the AWS list price = $79 / 1M tokens.
- Redwood net receipt: $395 - $79 = $316 / 1M tokens. This is the amount Redwood expects to receive as revenue per 1M tokens under the Marketplace flow.
- Invoice/billing flow: AWS bills PixlMedia per the private-offer unit price. AWS remits payment to Redwood net of Marketplace fee per AWS Marketplace settlement schedule.

Committed volume & discounts: Per Karthik's note we propose encoding the following ramped tiers in the private offer: 
  • 0 — 49.99M: $420 / 1M
  • 50M — 149.99M: $395 / 1M
  • 150M+: $365 / 1M
PixlMedia indicated intent to start at ~50M and move to ~90M; under the scheme above you will land in the $395 tier once you cross 50M. 

Next steps checklist: 
1) PixlMedia confirms the final committed baseline (we have 50M — 90M as possibilities). Please confirm the committed monthly floor for the PO.
2) PixlMedia signs the attached PO in DocuSign (link: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/agreements/DEAL-8672).
3) Redwood creates the AWS Private Offer listing reflecting the agreed tiers and unit price.
4) Procurement confirms AWS billing contact and we run a test settlement invoice in the first billing cycle.

Attachments: PixlMedia_PO_draft_8672.pdf (PO template), pricing_matrix.csv (sent earlier)

If you'd like I can change the wording in the mapping note to show a different marketplace fee assumption (eg 15% rather than 20%) — just let me know.
